deep.reconstruction:
This page is the blank side of a CRAY2 job printout dated 16 Aug 1982. The printout carries a French operator notice about a shutdown on 17 August, deletion of the spool disk, and the installation of new units from 20 to 23 August. It is used as scrap paper for the 1983–84 pseudo-line notes. The content is almost entirely drawings, with no running text.

(1) Top figure (green). Two pseudo-line branches cross at two points that are joined by a short segment, making an 'H'/tree-like shape. Thick black marks sit on the connecting edge and on two outer edges. This reads as a local picture of a degeneration: two crossings connected by a segment that can shrink. It could equally be a graph of specialisations whose edges carry lengths (marked edges = edges of length 1/2?).

(2) Middle figure. A green oriented pseudo-line (arrow pointing left) cuts three orange 'X's, each a pair of crossing pseudo-lines. In the middle X the green line passes exactly through the orange double point, giving a triple point, marked by a black dash. Faint grey arcs indicate the green line being pushed to either side of the crossings.

(3) Bottom figure. A second green oriented line cuts three orange X's. Thick black segments mark where the green line runs along or through the crossings. Thin black curved arrows show a deformation path of the line moving from below to above the crossings. A small annotation near the middle X (roughly '-1/2', '1/2', with small arrows) suggests half-unit lengths of specialisation arcs.

Modern reading: this is the local move in which one pseudo-line crosses the intersection point of two others, passing through a triple point. That is the triangle flip (mutation) between simple arrangements, i.e. a Reidemeister-III / braid-relation move. The marginal note, which appears to read σ1 σ2 σ1^{-1} (uncertain), fits a braid-word encoding of such a move. Together with the next page ('arc de spécialisation exceptionnel γ de longueur 0', segments of length 1/2, cases I_n, III_{p,q}), the purpose seems to be this: describe the stratified space of pseudo-line systems, or the specialisation graph between combinatorial types, near a non-simple configuration, and assign lengths to specialisation arcs. The bottom figure would then show the 1-parameter family through the degenerate (triple-point) arrangement and the specialisation arcs it creates.
errors: No checkable mathematical claim is written on the page; the drawings are consistent with the standard triangle-flip move.

ideas.what: Moving a pseudo-line across the crossing point of two others through a triple point (degenerate arrangement) and back
ideas.modern_name: Triangle flip / mutation of pseudoline arrangements; Reidemeister III; braid relation; codimension-one strata of the realization/combinatorial space
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ringel (1956, homotopy theorem); Goodman–Pollack; Manin–Schechtman (higher Bruhat orders, 1989)

ideas.what: Specialisation arcs between combinatorial types carrying lengths (1/2, 0), apparently drawn as thick marks on edges
ideas.modern_name: Metric on the poset/graph of specialisations of pseudo-line arrangements (stratified moduli of arrangements)

missed.claim: Across the neighbouring pages, Grothendieck appears to give specialisation arcs between pseudo-line configurations metric lengths (1/2, exceptional arcs of length 0). This page draws the local triple-point move these arcs come from. A metric structure on the space of pseudo-line arrangements of this kind is not standard in the oriented-matroid literature. This page alone only illustrates it, though.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It may relate to metric or tropical structures on moduli of arrangements. The evidence on this page is pictorial only.

deep.surprise_reason: These are drawings of the standard triangle-flip move for pseudoline arrangements. Any novelty lies in the surrounding 'length of specialisation arcs' framework, which is not stated on this page.
transcription_corrections: The printout banner date is '16 AUG 82'. The notice's items read: (1) shutdown on Tuesday 17 August from 7h to 8h; (2) deletion of spool disk contents on Tuesday 17 August at 6h; (3) exceptional shutdown from Friday 20 August 17h30 to Monday 23 August 8h for new units.
The handwritten annotations are sparse and rotated; the reading 'σ1 σ2 σ1^{-1}' is very uncertain. Near the middle X of the bottom figure there are small arrows and what looks like '1/2' or '-1/2'.

The main content consists of three colour drawings: a green two-node 'H' configuration with black marks, and two rows of a green oriented line through three orange X's, with black marks and thin curved deformation arrows.
